content:
Nearly two weeks after the Oct. 7 fire at the downtown DoubleTree Hotel, Laredo officials have an update on the burned-out building — and it is measured in weeks, not days.

Structural engineering firms from Maryland and Dallas, brought in by the building's owner, need five to six more weeks to assess the fire damage and investigate what caused it, KGNS reported Oct. 16. The current plan is stabilization, not demolition: Fire Chief Guillermo Heard said up to 20 to 30 or more pillars are expected to be installed to keep the 14-story structure standing. A companion KGNS video report by A.J. Juarez puts the same five-to-six-week timeline on the structural probe.

Here is what the engineers are dealing with: exposed rebar, sagging floors, and separation between walls and floors. The collapse zone was set at one and a half times the building's height. Nobody is allowed back inside — not even to retrieve documents or belongings. Barricades and road closures remain in place while the review is pending.

Mayor Dr. Victor Trevino extended the local emergency declaration through Oct. 23, and he drew the line where it ends: "If the building cannot be safely stabilized, we must move forward with a planned and coordinated demolition through the appropriate process." No costs for the assessment or the stabilization have been disclosed.

Meanwhile, downtown keeps bleeding

The longer the probe takes, the longer the barricades stay up — and the businesses trapped behind them keep paying. Rolando Sauceda, who has owned his restaurant on Constantinople Street for 32 years, told KGNS his sales have dropped, especially on Sundays when families used to fill the tables. He wants the city to help cover costs for businesses still unable to open. The Laredo Chamber of Commerce says impacted owners may qualify for SBA Economic Injury Disaster Loans — loans, not relief.

What Webb Watch is asking

Nine days after the fire, there is still no cause. There is no public cost estimate for the assessment, the pillars, or the eventual bill. There is no timeline for when the streets reopen. The building owner hired the engineers — but who is watching the timeline, and who holds them to it? The city has questions to answer, and downtown merchants do not have six more weeks of cash flow to spare. We will keep asking until the cause is named and the barricades come down.

Sources: KGNS (Elena Stoica), Oct. 16, 2026; KGNS (A.J. Juarez), Oct. 16, 2026; KGNS (Luis Enrique Vela), Oct. 12, 2026; Webb Watch 956 reporting.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Engineers need five to six more weeks to assess the burned DoubleTree and probe the fire's cause — while barricades stay up and downtown businesses keep losing money.
title: Five to Six More Weeks: The DoubleTree Probe Drags On While Downtown Businesses Bleed
